data.narrative:
Deep Atomic, a pre-seed nuclear energy company founded by William G.J. Theron, is evaluated against a comp universe of 10 peers: 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 7 private entities spanning the broader nuclear sector. The private peer set includes Helion, Oklo (pre-IPO phase), Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy, representing the most relevant trajectory comparables.

Traditional peer-median valuation methods are not applicable here. The nuclear energy sector contains only 6 same-sector peers overall, and filtering for pre-seed stage, adjacent financing rounds, or comparable valuation tiers yields fewer than 3 datapoints—below the threshold required for statistical reliability. A sector-wide median would conflate vastly different company maturities and capital requirements, rendering results uninformative for Deep Atomic's specific stage and risk profile.

Without sufficient narrow-stage comparables, this analysis cannot support a quantified valuation range. The dataset lacks the transaction multiples, recent funding rounds at pre-seed stage within nuclear energy, or revenue/development metrics necessary to triangulate via revenue multiples, precedent transactions, or venture capital method frameworks. A credible valuation would require either: (i) additional pre-seed or seed-stage nuclear peers with disclosed terms, (ii) operational metrics from Deep Atomic (R&D spend, IP claims, technical milestones), or (iii) explicit guidance on risk-adjusted cost-of-capital assumptions specific to pre-seed nuclear hardware ventures.
